name: Binance BTC/USDT multi-level taker sweep
description: Within one ingested Binance BTC/USDT trade batch sharing one event timestamp, aggressive flow on one side that consumes at or above min_levels (K) distinct prices is a sweep. detection_state is sweep when a side qualifies and quiet otherwise; a batch spanning exactly K-1 distinct prices does not fire. On detection the signal emits swept_levels (distinct prices consumed), swept_size (total consumed base size on that side), and direction (buy or sell). This is a state-shaped signal with a latest-sweep payload and a quiet default: the adopted spot set has no emit-only-on-detection signal to mirror, so a non-sweeping batch publishes detection_state = quiet and leaves the retained latest sweep unchanged. Every state-dependent field is always present: before any sweep has fired there is nothing retained, so the payload is the explicit sentinel direction = none with swept_levels 0 and swept_size 0 rather than a missing field. When both sides qualify in one batch the deeper level count wins, then the larger swept size, then buy, so the choice is deterministic. min_levels defaults to 3. This identity is single-venue by construction: the measurement compares one venue's own trades and book against each other, so it reads only Binance inputs and is ready whenever the Binance book-and-trade join is fresh, independently of the other adopted spot venue. No blended `btc.external.*` variant of this measurement is published: a cross-venue form would have to rule which venue's book prices another venue's trade, and that ruling is deferred pending evidence (ADR 0023 amendment and ADR 0024, both 2026-09-02). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even. Venue port (B1): this identity is the Binance sibling of `btc.coinbase.sweep_detection@1.0.0` and reuses that definition's formulas, windows, thresholds, warm-up, staleness bound, field set, field types and eight-place round-half-to-even rounding verbatim; only the source ids differ (`crates/btc-signals/src/spot_signals.rs`, `crates/btc-signals/src/candidate_spot_signals.rs`). The instrument is Binance spot BTCUSDT; this identity publishes no price-level field, so its outputs (base sizes, basis points, imbalances, ratios, counts) are quote-currency neutral and nothing is converted. Binance inputs are rights-gated (`signals/knowledge/RIGHTS-LEDGER.md`): the lane is built and tested to the adopted standard, and its runtime refuses to start unless the environment allow-list `SIGNALS_ENABLED_VENUES` names `binance`, which the deployment sets only after that row clears. The Binance book input is the `btcusdt@depth20@100ms` partial-depth stream: every message is a complete top-20-per-side image at a 100 ms cadence, not a diff, and it carries no venue clock, so `event_time_basis` is `receipt` and `event_time` is the local receipt time. Ordering is the strictly increasing `last_update_id`; a duplicate or lower id is dropped and never applied. The Binance trade input is the `btcusdt@aggTrade` stream: one message is an aggregate of fills at one price on one side at one `trade_time`, with `aggressor_side` derived from `buyer_is_maker`. Aggregation preserves price, side and time, so every formula over signed price-times-size is unchanged; `trade_count` fields count aggregate trades, not individual fills, and the identity states that. quote_currency is emitted on every decision and is the constant "usd" for this venue: this identity publishes no price-denominated field — its outputs are base sizes, ratios, basis-point and count fields, all quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted. E47 (USD quoting): this identity quotes in USD and publishes no price, notional or quote-denominated cost field — its outputs are base sizes, counts, basis-point ratios and durations, which are quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted and no usdt_usd_rate is published. quote_currency is the constant "usd".
